items.title: Chainlink
kv: Cross-system middleware for external data, verified messaging and coordinated execution.
It sits between systems that otherwise cannot safely observe or instruct one another, making it relevant wherever tokenized assets need prices, events, identity checks or cross-chain workflows.
A service network spanning oracle data, cross-chain messaging and workflow coordination rather than a single asset ledger.
Middleware can coordinate an instruction without becoming the issuer, custodian, transfer agent, settlement system or legal authority for the asset.

Independent node operators perform defined data or messaging jobs. · Data feeds aggregate external observations. · CCIP carries verified messages or token instructions across environments. · Connected institutions and ledgers complete the underlying asset and settlement actions.
Its service protocols and job execution, Message and data-delivery rules
Connected issuer liabilities, Destination-ledger finality, Legal title and cash discharge
Live middleware services with named integrations and separately bounded institutional programs.
Which messages trigger real settlement · Failure and recovery authority · Required LINK inventory versus optional service economics
Chainlink Labs ≠ every oracle node, CCIP message ≠ legal settlement, LINK ≠ the connected asset

items.title: chainlink · New build
kv: CCIP-supported mainnets (not individually named in the post)

Adds institution- or third-party-run Cross-Chain Verifiers that co-sign alongside the default verifier, an open verifier marketplace, issuer-set enforcement and configurable (faster-than-finality) confirmation, and Automated Compliance Engine integration. Chainlink lists launch partners/supporters including ANZ Bank, Fidelity International, Sygnum, SBI Digital Markets, Crypto Finance (Deutsche Boerse Group), Archax and others.

Self-reported figures ($84B cross-chain token value, $15B migrated) lack methodology. 'Launch partner/supporter' is not evidence each party moves value over CCIP 2.0. Ethereum Fast Confirmation support depends on a future Ethereum feature.

Verdict: confirmed · Evidence quote: Now live, CCIP 2.0 enables institutions to distribute tokenized assets across chains · Reason: Chainlink's own blog and release confirm that CCIP 2.0 is live, along with CCVs, the verifier marketplace, issuer-set enforcement, configurable finality, ACE, the named launch partners, and the self-reported $84B / $15B+. Entity note: 'Chainlink Labs' appears only in an executive's title; the site footer says Chainlink Foundation.
